claims.claim: Violations can trigger warning letters, daily fines, and in some cases, the HOA itself can coordinate towing at the homeowner's expense under Nevada Revised Statutes.
claims.notes: CORRECTED IN COPY 2026-09-06. The contradicted mechanism (driveway towing, daily fines) was removed from the live content and replaced with what NRS 116.3102/116.31031 support: fines per period after notice and a hearing opportunity, and towing limited to association property and community thoroughfares.
claims.contradiction: Two separate contradictions. (1) TOWING: NRS 116.3102 lets an association remove a vehicle improperly parked 'on property owned or leased by the association' or 'on any road, street, alley or other thoroughfare within the common-interest community'. A vehicle on the homeowner's own driveway is on the owner's lot — neither association property nor a thoroughfare — so the statute does not authorise the association to tow it. The live sentence attaches this power to 'a junk car sitting in your driveway'. (2) FINES: NRS 116.31031 permits an additional fine for each 7-DAY period after a violation is uncured for 14 days, not 'daily fines'. Fines are also capped at $100 per violation and $1,000 per hearing, and a hearing opportunity is required.
